# CircuitForge 0.20 digital peripherals

Original CC0 generic SVGs have explicit connector order. DHT bare packages use front 1 VCC / 2 DATA / 3 NC / 4 GND; NC has no internal electrical function. Breakouts and membrane headers vary across products; these drawings define their own labeled connector order.

- DHT11: 3–5.5 V, 1 s startup/read interval, ≥18 ms start; integer RH/T revision. DHT22/AM2302: 3.3–5.5 V, 1 s startup, ≥2 s reads, ≥1 ms start; tenths/sign-magnitude temperature. Response 30 µs delay, 80 µs LOW/HIGH, forty 50 µs LOW + 28/70 µs HIGH bits, final 50 µs LOW. Checksum is byte sum, not CRC. DATA is finite 100 Ω sink/release; an actual pull-up is required. Native examples use direct PIND polling and disabled interrupts. Startup events occur at AVR instruction boundaries, not UI frames. Environmental values are ideal samples; no accuracy/noise/heater model. [DHT11 manufacturer](https://www.adafruit.com/datasheets/DHT11-chinese.pdf), [AM2302](https://www.adafruit.com/datasheets/Digital%20humidity%20and%20temperature%20sensor%20AM2302.pdf), [Adafruit library](https://github.com/adafruit/DHT-sensor-library).
- HX711: original AVIA revision, wake resets A128. 25/26/27 clocks choose A128/B32/A64; signed 24-bit clipped conversion, ±0.5 AVDD/gain. RATE jumper 10/80 SPS, initial/channel settling 400/50 ms, subsequent 100/12.5 ms. >60 µs SCK HIGH powers down. Generic module ties AVDD/DVDD to VCC and E± through 0.1 Ω excitation links; it does not claim a specific 4.3 V regulator. A/B inputs use solved differential voltages and AGND+1.2…AVDD−1.3 common mode. Floating/out-of-range input flags `inputValid=false` and returns zero as an explicitly unsupported-input convention. Analog acquisition/noise/drift/oscillator variation are not modeled; subminimum clock timing is not rejected yet. [Original AVIA sheet](https://cdn.sparkfun.com/assets/0/2/7/d/1/HX711_datasheet.pdf). V2.0 retains setup after wake; that revision is not this model.
- Load cell: four passive bridge resistors R×(1±δ), δ=sensitivity(mV/V)×0.001×load/capacity, bounded ±0.1. Default 350 Ω, 2 mV/V at 1000 g; 500 g with 5 V excitation gives 5 mV differential before excitation loading. Four wires must be physically connected; reversing A± reverses the ADC sign. No direct weight-to-code shortcut, mechanical inertia, creep, temperature compensation or damage model. Parameters describe a generic calibrated bridge.
- TM1637: two-wire, LSB first, actual CLK↑ sampling and finite ACK sink. 0x40/0x44 data auto/fixed, C0–C5 RAM, display/shutdown/brightness duties [1,2,4,10,11,12,13,14]/16. Four visible digits; digit1 bit7 drives the central colon in this selected module variant. 0x42 returns FF because no key-scan terminals are exposed. Module has defined 10 kΩ CLK/DIO pullups and 1 kΩ logic load to prevent disconnected VCC phantom operation. Power loss clears RAM. No optical/current calibration. [Titan V2.4](https://m5stack.oss-cn-shenzhen.aliyuncs.com/resource/docs/datasheet/unit/digi_clock/TM1637.pdf), [Seeed](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/Grove-4-Digit_Display/).
- KY040: passive contacts CW (CLK,DT) 11→01→00→10→11; reverse CCW. Four 1 ms phases per detent. Switch closes SW→GND. External Uno INPUT_PULLUP used; no universal onboard pull-up or manufacturer detent-count claim. Contacts operate without VCC when ground and pullups are connected. No bounce model. [Joy-IT](https://sensorkit.joy-it.net/en/sensors/ky-040).
- Keypad: eight passive R1…4/C1…4 terminals, each selected key stamps a 0.05 Ω contact. Click/Enter toggles each contact independently; multiple keys can remain pressed. No diodes/debounce; ghosting follows actual matrix/pull-up electrical paths. Different real membranes use different connector orders. [Adafruit pinouts](https://learn.adafruit.com/matrix-keypad/pinouts), [Microchip AN3407](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/MCU08/ApplicationNotes/ApplicationNotes/00003407A.pdf).

All device event callbacks are invalidated on removal/power loss/disposal. Newly selected projects and Run/reset create fresh controllers. Existing circuit transport and firmware/source validation are preserved.
